name: Oral-only cycle

card.summary: A course of anabolic steroids taken only as tablets, with no injectable base, which people use in hopes of adding muscle and a fuller physique.
card.note: Oral anabolic steroids are controlled drugs in many countries; 17-alpha-alkylated orals are linked to liver effects.

quick.overview:
An oral-only cycle is a course of performance- and appearance-enhancing drugs, usually anabolic-androgenic steroids, taken exclusively as pills or capsules rather than injections. People use it to add muscle size, density and definition faster than training alone.

Its appeal described on forums is convenience and shorter courses, and some members claim shorter oral courses may reduce hormonal suppression. Forum accounts are anecdotal; research on this specific pattern is limited, and the general effects of steroids are documented in medical literature.
quick.how: On forums, members describe short courses of one or more tablet steroids, often alongside post-course recovery drugs. Specific compounds, doses and schedules are not covered here. Results are reported over weeks, and members describe gains as partly water weight and often temporary after stopping.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroids are controlled substances in many countries, including Schedule III in the US. Oral 17-alpha-alkylated compounds are associated with liver enzyme elevations and other liver effects. All anabolic steroids can suppress natural testosterone production, affect cholesterol and blood pressure, and cause acne and mood effects. Medical supervision and bloodwork are generally advised by clinicians.

lead: An oral-only cycle, also called "orals only", is a pattern of anabolic-androgenic steroid use in which only tablet or capsule compounds are used, without an injectable testosterone base.[1]

People in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing communities describe it as a way to build muscle, size and definition. A frequently stated rationale among forum members is that short courses limit the hormonal "crash" afterwards, while others consider orals-only courses counterintuitive without a testosterone base.
Medical references document that oral steroids are modified at the 17-alpha position so they survive passage through the liver, and that this class is associated with liver effects.[1]

chain: More muscle protein synthesis alongside training
angle.text: Anabolic steroids are used to increase muscle size and definition, and the oral-only pattern is one way people pursue this. Gains are often reported to fade after the course ends.

infobox: Controlled substances in many countries (US Schedule III)
Liver effects with 17-alpha-alkylated orals; hormonal suppression

paras: The pattern is defined by what it leaves out: no injected steroid, usually no testosterone base. Forum members describe it as a short course of orals followed by recovery medication, and some attribute the approach to sprinters and coaches, a claim made by forum posters.

Some members say short oral-only courses gave their best response and that injectable gains plateau after the first weeks; others say running orals without a base is counterintuitive. These are anecdotal accounts.

Testosterone taken by mouth is largely converted to inactive metabolites, so oral steroids such as methyltestosterone and fluoxymesterone are alkylated at the 17-alpha position, which slows liver breakdown.[1] Wikipedia's summary says orally available steroids may cause liver damage in high doses, with raised liver enzymes, jaundice, cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and hepatic tumours reported mostly with this class.[1]

Anabolic steroids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis in men in a dose-dependent way, which can lead to testicular atrophy and reduced sperm production; after a short course, clomifene or hCG therapy usually restores production.[1] Other documented effects include unfavourable cholesterol changes, hypertension, acne, gynecomastia and psychiatric effects.[1] The IARC lists anabolic steroids as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans).[1]

Anabolic steroids are Schedule III controlled substances in the US, Class C in the UK and Schedule IV in Canada, and they are banned in most sport; where controlled, a black market exists for counterfeit and smuggled products.[1]
No studies found on oral-only cycles as a pattern. Medical literature on anabolic steroids in general is summarised in reference articles.[1]

lore.intro: Oral-only cycles are discussed on looksmax.org and in T Nation threads as an alternative to injectable-based courses.

claims.claim: Short oral-only courses limit hormonal suppression
claims.believers: Forum posters say short course length and timing of dosing are meant to minimise the effect on the hypothalamus.
claims.experts: Anabolic steroids suppress the HPG axis in a dose-dependent way, and recovery therapy is typically needed after short courses.[1]

claims.claim: Oral-only courses give good short-term results
claims.believers: Some members say short oral-only courses gave their best response and that injectables plateau after the first weeks.
claims.experts: No published studies have compared oral-only patterns with other regimens; liver effects are documented for 17-alpha-alkylated orals.[1]
